\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{مرداب} (mordâb)}{مرداب (mordâb)}]{\fa{مرداب} (mordâb) — a marsh, a swamp}

\label{lesson:FA-C469-mordab}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for the foothills, then the Persian for to climb.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{مرداب}}
\textbf{\fa{مرداب}} (\emph{mordâb}) — \textquotedblleft{}a marsh, a swamp\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{پرنده} \fa{های} \fa{زیادی} \fa{در} \fa{مرداب} \fa{زندگی} \fa{میکنند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Parande-hâ-ye ziyâdi dar mordâb zendegi mikonand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Many birds live in the marsh.
\end{quote}

Literally 'dead water': \emph{mord} 'dead' + \emph{âb} 'water'.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{mordâb} is usually analysed as native \emph{mord} 'dead', from \emph{mordan} 'to die', and \emph{âb} 'water', from Middle Persian \emph{āb} (EtymDB): still, standing water.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mordâb}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mordâb}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{mordâb}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for the foothills, then the Persian for to climb, then say \emph{mordâb} again
\end{itemize}

\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{تالاب} (tâlâb)}{تالاب (tâlâb)}]{\fa{تالاب} (tâlâb) — a wetland, a lagoon}

\label{lesson:FA-C469-talab}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to climb, then the Persian for a marsh.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{تالاب}}
\textbf{\fa{تالاب}} (\emph{tâlâb}) — \textquotedblleft{}a wetland, a lagoon\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{پرنده} \fa{ها} \fa{زمستان} \fa{را} \fa{در} \fa{تالاب} \fa{میگذرانند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Parande-hâ zemestân râ dar tâlâb migozarânand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The birds spend the winter in the wetland.
\end{quote}

Iran's wetlands are winter homes for many birds from the north.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{tâlâb} is a native word, which EtymDB derives from \emph{âb} 'water', itself from Middle Persian \emph{āb}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tâlâb}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{tâlâb}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to climb, then the Persian for a marsh, then say \emph{tâlâb} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{نهر} (nahr)}{نهر (nahr)}]{\fa{نهر} (nahr) — a stream, a brook; a channel}

\label{lesson:FA-C469-nahr}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a marsh, then the Persian for a wetland.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{نهر}}
\textbf{\fa{نهر}} (\emph{nahr}) — \textquotedblleft{}a stream, a brook; a channel\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{کنار} \fa{نهر} \fa{نشستیم} \fa{و} \fa{چای} \fa{خوردیم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Kenâr-e nahr neshastim va chây khordim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We sat by the stream and drank tea.
\end{quote}

In Arabic \emph{nahr} is a river; in Persian a smaller stream.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{nahr} was borrowed from Arabic \emph{nahr} 'river' (EtymDB); in Persian it names a stream or a channel.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{سد} (sadd)}{سد (sadd)}]{\fa{سد} (sadd) — a dam}

\label{lesson:FA-C469-sadd}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a wetland, then the Persian for a stream.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{سد}}
\textbf{\fa{سد}} (\emph{sadd}) — \textquotedblleft{}a dam\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{پشت} \fa{سد} \fa{یک} \fa{دریاچه} \fa{بزرگ} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Posht-e sadd yek daryâche-ye bozorg ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Behind the dam there is a big lake.
\end{quote}

Also a barrier: \emph{sadd-e râh} — an obstacle.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{sadd} was borrowed from Arabic \emph{sadd} 'dam, barrier' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{جاری} \fa{شدن} (jâri shodan)}{جاری شدن (jâri shodan)}]{\fa{جاری} \fa{شدن} (jâri shodan) — to flow, to run (of water)}

\label{lesson:FA-C469-jari-shodan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a stream, then the Persian for a dam.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{جاری} \fa{شدن}}
\textbf{\fa{جاری} \fa{شدن}} (\emph{jâri shodan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to flow, to run (of water)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{بعد} \fa{از} \fa{باران} \fa{آب} \fa{در} \fa{جوب} \fa{جاری} \fa{شد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Ba'd az bârân âb dar jub jâri shod.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
After the rain water ran in the gutter.
\end{quote}

\emph{jâri} 'flowing' + \emph{shodan}. \emph{Âb-e jâri} — running water.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{jâri shodan} is built from \emph{jâri} 'flowing', borrowed from Arabic \emph{jārī} (EtymDB), and the native verb \emph{shodan} 'to become'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
